vedic_reference.note: Dhruva is the name of a star, the Pole Star, and the name of a famous devotee in Bhagavata Purana.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dhruvanya" holds a rich heritage in Hindu mythology. It is derived from the ancient story of King Dhruva, who renounced his kingdom and underwent severe penance in order to regain a place in the cosmos. This name carries a deep sense of unwavering focus, determination, and devotion to one's goals, as embodied by King Dhruva's unwavering star.
data.spiritual_significance: At its core, the name "Dhruvanya" represents a profound spiritual connection to unwavering faith and determination, inspired by the celestial figure of Dhruva. It serves as a reminder that no matter the challenges faced on one's spiritual journey, maintaining unwavering commitment and focus keeps us on the path towards Enlightenment. Inner strength and perseverance, highlighted in this name, are essential qualities for personal transformation and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, King Dhruva was an ungrateful prince who was cursed by his father to wander the earth as a star named Dhruva. This occurred during the Treta Yuga, around 3000-2500 BCE.
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology and ancient Indian history

historical_references.reference: The sage Markandeya mentions Dhruvanya, a human being who attained the supreme goal in life and merged into the cosmic self, in his epic text, the Markandeya Purana. The exact time period of this reference is not mentioned but it is believed to belong to the later periods of Hinduism, around 200 CE.

Lastly, on blogs and websites, there are articles and resources that explore the deeper meaning of the name 'Dhruvanya' in relation to mental health and personal growth. Overall, the use of 'Dhruvanya' in modern context serves as a reminder of the importance of staying steadfast in one's beliefs and seeking inner peace and guidance.
